name: A11y
description: Accessible writing: alt text, link text, heading structure, table headers, instructions that rely on color or position, a reading grade per paragraph, and an inclusive-language word list, from the parts of WCAG 2.2 that live in the text.

name: APIDocs
description: The prose in OpenAPI documents: operation summaries and descriptions, parameter and property descriptions, and terms, read through a View that ships with the package.

name: AiTells
description: Flags the tells of AI-written prose: em-dash habits, epigrams, abstract-noun triads, clichés, and 13 more benchmarked rules.

name: AsciiDoc
description: A Vale-compatible implementation of select AsciiDoc syntax rules.

name: AsciiDocDITA
description: A Vale-compatible implementation of select DITA transformation guidelines for transforming existing AsciiDoc files into a DITA-compatible format.

name: Changelog
description: Changelogs in the Keep a Changelog format: release headings, ISO dates, the six change types, and vague entries, with an opt-in style for release-note tone.

name: Comments
description: The comments in code: Go doc comments, Javadoc, and KDoc conventions, plus owned TODOs and no commented-out code in any language Vale extracts comments from.

name: Commits
description: Commit messages: nine conventions and the rule sets of commitlint, gitlint, committed, conform, and commitizen, read through a View.

name: Diataxis
description: The four kinds of documentation in Diátaxis, each checked against its job: tutorials that walk, how-to guides that reach a goal, reference that describes, explanation that answers why.

name: Elastic
description: Elastic Docs' style guide rules for the Vale linter.

name: Fiction
description: Fiction: filter words, told emotions, stock phrases, and dialogue punctuation, with the rules of Elmore Leonard, Chuck Palahniuk, and Strunk's 1918 Elements of Style.

name: GlobalEnglish
description: English for translation and for readers whose first language isn't English: idioms, phrasal verbs, Latin abbreviations, ambiguous words, and an opt-in style for procedures in controlled English.

name: Google
description: A Vale-compatible implementation of the Google Developer Documentation Style Guide.

name: Harper
description: A Vale-compatible implementation of the Harper grammar checker.

name: Hugo
description: Adds support for Hugo shortcodes and other non-standard markup.

name: Joblint
description: Test tech job posts for issues with sexism, culture, expectations, and recruiter fails.

name: Journals
description: Scientific manuscripts: a core of conventions for units, statistics, figures, and citations, the IMRaD structure, the Nature and PLOS ONE author guidelines, and the CONSORT, STROBE, and PRISMA checklists.

name: MDX
description: Adds support for MDX comments and other non-standard markup.

name: Microcopy
description: UI text: sentence-case labels, specific button verbs, error messages that blame or say nothing, filler, and confirmations, with a View for i18n locale files.

name: Microsoft
description: A Vale-compatible implementation of the Microsoft Writing Style Guide.

name: OpenShiftAsciiDoc
description: A Vale-compatible implementation of select AsciiDoc guidance from the OpenShift docs contributor guidelines.

name: PlainLanguage
description: The US Federal Plain Language Guidelines: simple words, hidden verbs, jargon, "must" over "shall", double negatives, passive voice, and sentence length.

name: Prompts
description: Lints instruction files such as AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and SKILL.md: advice in place of commands, vague verbs, contradictions, too much emphasis, and files too long to read on every turn.

name: Readability
description: Readability scores: Automated Readability Index, Coleman-Liau, Flesch-Kincaid, Flesch reading ease, Gunning fog, LIX, and SMOG, with a rule that names the polysyllables behind them.

name: RedHat
description: A Vale-compatible implementation of the Red Hat Supplementary Style Guide.

name: Salesforce
description: A Vale-compatible implementation of the Salesforce Writing Style Guide.

name: Std
description: The standard library for Vale: general-purpose rules you extend to build your own style.

name: TechTerms
description: A spelling dictionary of 115,000 technical terms, from product and company names to file types and the vocabulary of some 30 programming languages, built from cspell's MIT-licensed word lists. Vale.Spelling uses it beside its own dictionary.

name: Voices
description: Writing voices as Vale rules: a shared core against hedging, puffery, weasel words, and throat clearing, and voices such as Direct, Simple, and Human that set how the prose should sound.

name: ai-tells
description: Flags the fingerprints of AI-written prose, with rule messages that name the fix rather than only the phrase.

name: alex
description: Catch insensitive, inconsiderate writing.

name: neighbor
description: Accessibility and inclusive language rules for Vale. Flags exclusionary language, ableist terms, metaphors, and complex idioms.

name: proselint
description: proselint places the world’s greatest writers and editors by your side.

name: write-good
description: Naive linter for English prose for developers who can't write good.
